source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Projection, in which the person attributes unacceptable thoughts or feelings of their own to somebody else.","B":"Sublimation, in which unacceptable impulses are redirected toward socially acceptable activities or goals.","C":"Rationalization, in which the person offers plausible explanations to justify behavior or feelings after the fact.","D":"Regression, in which stress is associated with a return to coping behaviors characteristic of an earlier stage."}}
source_row.rationale: Regression is an often-unconscious return to earlier or less mature patterns of behavior under stress; it should not automatically be labeled intentional attention-seeking or malingering.
source_row.source_detail: Defense-mechanism table defines regression as reverting to an earlier stage or less mature behavior in response to anxiety or stress. Open RN psychiatric nursing content, 2025 NCBI Bookshelf edition; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: During a stressful hospitalization, an adult begins using markedly childlike and dependent behaviors. Which defense mechanism may explain this response?
